rendered: NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated at a pH window between 10 and 12[1]. The reason is that the constituent metals do not precipitate together easily. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is challenging because of the varying solubility product Ksp of their hydroxides.[2][3] Aluminum hydroxide starts precipitating at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate only beyond pH 6[4].[5][6] This narrows the coprecipitation window to the range above, which is the window for successful synthesis of NFA precursors as hydroxides. In practice, NaOH is pumped into the continuous stirred tank reactor to hold the pH above 10[7], especially for nickel-rich materials.[8][9] To turn the precursors into cathode powder, the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors. These are mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures >600 °C[10].[11][12][13] After calcination, the NFA cathode powder is cast into electrodes by roll-to-roll slot-die coating.[14][15]
